_meta.indication: CALQUENCE is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with mantle cell lymphoma (MCL) who have received at least one prior therapy; approved under accelerated approval based on overall response rate

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 2, multicenter, single-arm, open-label study; acalabrutinib 100 mg orally twice daily until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with relapsed or refractory mantle cell lymphoma who had received at least one prior therapy; median age 68 years, median number of prior therapies 2; prior BTK inhibitor treatment excluded
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Overall response rate (ORR) per investigator assessment using the 2014 Lugano Classification for Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma
pivotal_trials.result: ORR 80.6% (95% CI: 72.6, 87.2) by investigator assessment; complete response rate 39.5% (95% CI: 30.9, 48.7); median duration of response not reached with median follow-up of 15.2 months

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥20% of patients) were anemia, thrombocytopenia, headache, neutropenia, diarrhea, fatigue, myalgia, and bruising. In the combined safety database (n=612): Grade 3 or 4 cytopenias including neutropenia (23%), anemia (11%) and thrombocytopenia (8%); Grade 3 or higher infections in 18%; second primary malignancies in 11%; atrial fibrillation and flutter in 3%
target_moa: Acalabrutinib is a Bruton tyrosine kinase (BTK) inhibitor that forms a covalent bond with the cysteine residue (Cys481) in the BTK active site, leading to inhibition of BTK enzymatic activity

rems.type: No REMS indicated; safe use can be managed through accurate labeling and routine hematology and oncology care

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because it did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues in the intended population

summary.text: Acalabrutinib received Orphan Drug Designation (2015) and Breakthrough Therapy Designation (2017) for mantle cell lymphoma, was reviewed under Priority review, and was granted accelerated approval under 21 CFR 314.510 based on the surrogate endpoint of overall response rate, with a required confirmatory randomized trial to verify clinical benefit

citations.quote: September 21, 2015	Orphan Drug Designation granted for mantle cell lymphoma.
July 31, 2017	Breakthrough Therapy Designation granted for the treatment of patients with mantle cell lymphoma (MCL) who have received at least one prior therapy.

The review team recommends accelerated approval of acalabrutinib under 21 CFR 314.510 Subpart H for the indication “for treatment of adult patients with mantle cell lymphoma who have received at least one prior therapy.”
